text:
alice: Heads-up — kernel 6.4.8 rollout in eu-west-2 is causing some hosts with P4s to fail NVIDIA module load during boot. Seen on two racks so far.
raj: Observed same in staging after a canary. dmesg shows repeated BAR0/PCIe AER errors then nvidia_module: failed to init.
cheng: can you paste the exact dmesg snippet? trying to see if it's the same signature as last time.
alice: paste below — short:
```
[  12.345678] pci 0000:38:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error: Multiple Uncorr Error
[  12.345679] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel.
[ 12.346000] nvidia: probe of 0000:38:00.0 failed with error -5
[ 12.346100] pcieport 0000:3e:00.0: AER: device recovery failed
```
irenE: @alice minor nit — i think you meant irene :)
irene: thanks. looks like this is different from the 6.3 nccl timeout case, this is early in boot. error -5 is EIO.
raj: could be the nvidia module ABI mismatch with the new kernel headers. Which distro/kernel packaging did this batch use?
alice: ubuntu-22.04 with our 6.4.8 build from kernel-team. DKMS builds succeeded but at runtime it crashes on pcie init.
cheng: DKMS sometimes hides build-time success but the kernel config or KMS interface changed. Quick mitigation: pin kernel to 5.15 for affected node pool and revert the upgrade job.
oncall: rolling back can be heavy — capacity hit if we don't evacuate GPU pods first. we saw NCCL heartbeats drop before pods crashed in staging.
raj: suggestion: cordon affected hosts, drain GPU pods (prefer preemption) and shift to spare capacity in us-west while we triage. Need a rollback playbook if bulk failure.
alice: draining now on the two racks. starting live-migrate for critical workloads.
irene: for triage, can someone try booting a host with the 6.4 image but with nvidia module blacklisted to see if the machine boot completes? if yes, confirms module as root cause.
cheng: i can repro on a spare node. will try manual boot with modprobe.blacklist=nvidia and report.
deploy-bot: [deploy] kernel-upgrade-job eu-west-2 started for batch-42 (id: kj-042)
raj: if blacklist lets it boot, we can at least get SSH and grab kernel logs, then attempt a manually-built driver (from our pinned driver tree) and insmod to see failure mode.
cheng: quick test: blacklisting nvidia -> boots, but then pods that need GPU fail as expected. insmod of our driver binary yields:
```
insmod: init_module 'nvidia': Unsupported relocation type
```
cheng: that suggests differences in GCC or kernel module symbol layout.
irene: possible regressions introduced by recent CONFIG options in 6.4 that affect module relocation. we'll open a kernel-team ticket.
oncall: ops question — do we have enough spare capacity if rollback is required? current spare GPUs across regions are ~10% per finance report. if we pull eu-west racks offline we'll hit SLAs for some customers.
alice: agreed. starting AC/PG to prioritize critical customers and shift low-priority workloads.
raj: next steps: (1) stall further 6.4 rollouts, (2) repro on spare with debug symbols, (3) engage kernel-team and nvidia-driver owners, (4) prepare rollback playbook and customer comms.
cheng: I'll attach logs and the insmod trace to the ticket. also want to test booting with CONFIG_RELOCATABLE enabled/disabled kernels.
irene: FYI NCCL churn we observed — after module failures some services show nccl handshake timeouts and gdr errors; may need to re-run NCCL health checks post-recovery.
alice: thanks everyone. I'll update oncall and create a short incident channel if we escalate. :warning:
oncall: noted. creating #incident/eu-west-kernel-nv  — joining: @alice @raj @cheng @irene
deploy-bot: [alert] rollback-playbook template copied to /runbooks/rollback-kernel-nvidia.md
alice: copying final note — if you see hosts with "Failed to allocate BAR region" in dmesg, do not reboot repeatedly; cordon + drain is preferred.
cheng: will send a short postmortem draft after we stabilize.
alice: end of thread for now — will post updates in #incident/eu-west-kernel-nv
